# University of the Andes (Colombia) – Key Information
The University of the Andes (Colombia), known as Uniandes, was founded in 1948 and began classes in 1949 as the nation’s first nonsectarian and non-politically affiliated university, modeled after the American university college. Established as a nonprofit corporation and granted university status in 1964, Uniandes aimed to provide technical and liberal education to develop professionals and leaders for Colombia. Located in the historical center of Bogotá, the campus includes renovated industrial and religious buildings as well as modern facilities, with extensive classrooms, laboratories, libraries, sports, and health services. Notably, the mascot is a goat named Seneca, and students celebrate "Students' Day" in its honor.
Governance is overseen by the Board of Trustees and Board of Directors, supported by the Rector and Academic Council. The university consists of 14 academic units—including 10 faculties—and 20 administrative units, with a diverse staff and significant financial assets. Uniandes offers an interdisciplinary curriculum allowing students flexibility in course selection across four academic cycles (basic, elective socio-humanistic, professional, and professional complementary). As of recent data, 55% of its students are male, 45% female, with 30% originating outside Bogotá and 95% of undergraduates ranking in the top 1% nationally. The faculty is predominantly full-time, with 70% holding PhDs from prestigious global universities, and the institution maintains active academic exchange programs with over 119 universities in 34 countries. Prominent alumni include political leaders, artists, scientists, and public figures from Colombia.
